title: A right to the work, and an even mind

verses.sa: व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन । बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥
verses.tr: O son of the Kurus, the resolute intellect is one-pointed here. The intellect of the irresolute is many-branched and endless.
verses.angle: bahusakhah, many branches, of the irresolute mind
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna sets up a stark choice between the mind that knows its target and the mind that cannot stop branching out. Listen for the word that names the endless path.

body.text: O son of the Kurus, the resolute intellect is one-pointed here. The intellect of the irresolute is many-branched and endless. Krishna contrasts the resolute mind, aimed one way, with the irresolute mind branching endlessly. Krishna now explains that people with this scattered mind speak empty words about the Vedas, missing the truth entirely.

verses.sa: यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः । वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः ॥
verses.tr: The unwise speak flowery words. They delight in the ritual sections of the Vedas and say nothing else exists.
verses.angle: Pushpitam: flowery speech that dresses up craving
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna points to a certain kind of talk that sounds sacred but hides a shallow aim. Listen for the word that marks it.

body.text: The unwise speak flowery words. They delight in the ritual sections of the Vedas and say nothing else exists. The word is pushpitam, flowery. These people dress up desire in polished, sacred language and treat reward-seeking as the whole of life, closing their minds to anything beyond it. Krishna immediately adds that this speech promises birth and action-fruit, describing many rites for enjoyment.

verses.sa: कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम् । क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति ॥
verses.tr: Those without clear seeing speak flowery words that promise birth and action-fruit, and describe many rites for enjoyment and power.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now names the listeners he is speaking to, the ones who get caught in flowery words. Listen for the mark of a teaching that keeps a person bound.

body.text: Those without clear seeing speak flowery words that promise birth and action-fruit, and describe many rites for enjoyment and power. Listen to the word kamatmanah, those whose minds are full of desire. It marks the speakers and the listeners, showing that a teaching born from craving can only offer more craving, birth, and action. Krishna then shows what happens when the mind is carried away by pleasure and power.

verses.sa: भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम् । व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥
verses.tr: For those whose minds are carried away by pleasure and power, steadfast determination in meditation does not arise.
verses.angle: buddhi: the intellect that cannot settle
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just finished describing the flowery words of those who promise rewards. He now explains why the mind cannot hold steady.

body.text: For those whose minds are carried away by pleasure and power, steadfast determination in meditation does not arise. The intellect, buddhi, is not established in steady meditation because the mind has been stolen by the attraction to pleasure and power. Krishna then tells Arjuna to rise above the three qualities and beyond opposites like gain and loss.

verses.sa: त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन । निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान् ॥
verses.tr: The Vedas deal with the three qualities. Arjuna, rise beyond the three qualities, beyond opposites, fixed in lasting reality, free from concern for gain and security, and established in the true self.
verses.angle: Niryogakshema: stop worrying about gain and loss
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna is paralyzed by grief, and Krishna points to a way out. What is it that he must stop doing? Listen for the instruction.

body.text: The Vedas deal with the three qualities. Arjuna, rise beyond the three qualities, beyond opposites, fixed in lasting reality, free from concern for gain and security, and established in the true self. The word niryogakshema means free from worry about gaining things or protecting them. Krishna tells Arjuna to stop chasing security and comfort, and instead root himself in the unchanging self. Krishna explains that this inner freedom makes the vast Vedas as small as a puddle compared to the ocean of knowledge.

verses.sa: यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः संप्लुतोदके । तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः ॥
verses.tr: For one who understands, all the Vedas are as useful as a small puddle when a great reservoir of water is at hand.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna shifts from rules to a single image of water. Listen for how one full reservoir makes a puddle unnecessary.

body.text: For one who understands, all the Vedas are as useful as a small puddle when a great reservoir of water is at hand. One Sanskrit word, udapane, means a small puddle. When a person stands beside a great reservoir that is full from all sides, that puddle offers nothing more. Krishna then tells Arjuna that his right is only to work, never to the results.

verses.sa: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verses.tr: You have a right to action alone, never to its fruits. Do not become the cause of the result, and do not cling to inaction.
verses.angle: Karma: the anchor of the verse
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna gives a hard line about what belongs to you and what does not. Listen for the word that appears three times and holds the whole verse together.

body.text: You have a right to action alone, never to its fruits. Do not become the cause of the result, and do not cling to inaction. The word karma, action, appears three times here. It is the only thing that is yours to own, while the fruits and the cause of the fruits are not. Krishna now tells Arjuna to perform these actions while remaining established in yoga, equal in success and failure.

verses.sa: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
verses.tr: O Dhananjaya, perform actions while established in yoga, abandoning attachment. Remain equal in success and failure, for equanimity is called yoga.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has told Arjuna to act, but not to crave the results. Now he gives the precise inner state that makes that action true yoga. Listen to how he defines it.

body.text: O Dhananjaya, perform actions while established in yoga, abandoning attachment. Remain equal in success and failure, for equanimity is called yoga. Krishna does not define yoga as a posture or a breath. He defines it as samatvam, evenness. The exact moment of success or failure does not have to shake the one who is established in yoga. Krishna now contrasts that steady state with action born of craving, and calls the craving-driven path pitiful. Listen.

verses.sa: दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय । बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥
verses.tr: Action driven by craving is far below the steadiness of clear discernment. Seek refuge in clear discernment, for those who chase results are pitiable.
verses.angle: Kripanah: pitiful, the word for the reward-driven
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna carries the teaching forward, contrasting two kinds of action and the mind that guides them.

body.text: Action driven by craving is far below the steadiness of clear discernment. Seek refuge in clear discernment, for those who chase results are pitiable. The word kripanah means pitiable. Krishna calls those who chase results pitiable because their happiness depends on outcomes they cannot control. Krishna then explains how one united with discernment casts off both good and bad deeds in this life.

verses.sa: बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते । तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥
verses.tr: One who is united with clear discernment casts off both good and bad deeds in this life. Therefore, devote yourself to yoga, for yoga is skill in action.
verses.angle: yuktasva: be devoted, and yoga is skill
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna answers the fear of doing wrong: a steady mind changes how action binds. Listen for the reason he gives.

body.text: One who is united with clear discernment casts off both good and bad deeds in this life. Therefore, devote yourself to yoga, for yoga is skill in action. The word yuktasva, be devoted, appears twice in this verse. First he tells Arjuna to be devoted to yoga, and then he defines yoga itself as skill in action. Krishna then explains how those united in wisdom reach a flawless state, free from the bondage of birth.

verses.sa: कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः । जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम् ॥
verses.tr: Wise people, united in clarity, abandon the fruit born of action and reach the flawless state, free from the bondage of birth.
verses.angle: Gacchanti: moving toward a flawless state
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna speaks of a release that comes not from stopping action, but from letting go of what action produces. Listen to how the wise reach it.

body.text: Wise people, united in clarity, abandon the fruit born of action and reach the flawless state, free from the bondage of birth. The verb is gacchanti, they go. The wise do not stay still; they move toward a flawless state, a place without affliction, simply by abandoning the fruit of what they do. Krishna now turns to the intellect itself, saying that when it crosses delusion, it grows dispassionate.

verses.sa: यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति । तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥
verses.tr: When your intellect crosses the swamp of delusion, you will grow dispassionate toward what has been heard and what remains to be heard.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna tells Arjuna that the root of his confusion is a swamp. Listen for the word that names this swamp.

body.text: When your intellect crosses the swamp of delusion, you will grow dispassionate toward what has been heard and what remains to be heard. Listen for moha, delusion. Krishna does not call it a thought or a feeling; he calls it a swamp. Once your intellect crosses it, the pull of promised pleasures simply drops away. Next, Krishna describes the steady mind that has already crossed this swamp.

verses.sa: श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला । समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥
verses.tr: When your intellect, unmoved by conflicting teachings, becomes steady in complete stillness, you will attain yoga.
verses.angle: Samadhi: the stillness of the intellect
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna, taking him past the confusion of different teachings so he can see what a steady mind truly looks like.

body.text: When your intellect, unmoved by conflicting teachings, becomes steady in complete stillness, you will attain yoga. The word samadhi, complete stillness, names the exact state where the intellect finally arrives. It is not a vague calm, but the mind resting completely in one place. Arjuna asks what a person of steady wisdom looks like in daily life, and how they speak, sit, and walk.
